summary: Android's dev.boardcraft.BROWSE action opens a read-only picker with the existing origin-scoped session. Kit buttons call EditClient::read_selected_board with the tapped board UUID. The host checks current access on each read; Back and Refresh call list_boards without replaying a selection.
evidence: Prior packet 24 emulator run: after masked sign-in, foreground frames showed Quartz, Review, Review. Tapping the second Review showed Sketch above Ink; Android Back returned to the list, and tapping the first Review showed Outline alone.

In that run the fixture removed workspace membership after the list appeared. The stale second tap showed Destination unavailable without protected rows. Android Back showed No boards. Restoring membership and tapping Refresh displayed the ordered list; only a new tap reopened Sketch and Ink.

At nine checkpoints in that run, fresh database connections confirmed the original session and account, all three subscriptions, the expected membership, and unchanged ordered items: 73 Sketch then 61 Ink on the selected board, and 62 Outline on its sibling, all at revision 1. The offline frame and direct board/port edit gates also passed in the prior run.

This retry: all eight loopback_board_access cases passed, including selected_board_read_checks_current_membership. The locked workspace suite passed all 22 tests. All 13 serial Windows smoke cases passed, including opens_selected_board_by_id and revoked_membership_blocks_board_selection. Both Cargo formatting checks and git diff --check passed.

The worker shell denied the Node runner regression and Android browse commands on this retry; there is no fresh device result. The prior reference comparison covered UUID selection and Back handling. The picker has one prior screen; full Home/history, physical gestures and browse-specific cold restore remain unverified.
next: Run the registered packet 24 verification gate on the exclusive x86_64 fixture AVD.
